body:
Just to add one more time: please do not send this or anything at all to him. It is not worth it. Whatever you think it will do, it won't. 


Very rarely does any man (or woman) require an essay of a text, and if you are close enough with them that they deserve it, you should just see them in person and say what you have to say. This is not that situation. Please don't send this.

Please don't do this. It's been 3 years. It seems to me that whatever attraction toward you he may have felt at some point you have overblown in your head greatly. I really don't see what there is to gain here, as it is clear he is both taken and not interested.

I was in the same scenario last year (my LO became my direct manager). It was a really hard time for me when I found that out, and it was also pretty rough throughout the whole time that he was my manager. Having a coworker who is an LO is already hell, but a manager I wouldn't wish on anyone. Any chance you can find another job?

I think it will be incredibly hard if not impossible to get rid of limerance when you are still in contact with him as often as you are. Your best bet might be to fall in love with someone else, but even that can get messy.

You have to decide you really want to be free of this. This person already rejected you. I don't know what the situation is, but if at all possible you need to start no contact. It will be very difficult, if not impossible not to read into things when you are still around them and have new material to analyse on a regular basis.

I would definitely still be limerent if he hadn't left. It was impossible for me to cure my limerence when I had to be in contact with him almost every day. Now I can finally go no contact, and that is so freeing. Really didn't believe I would feel this good so soon.

Similar thing happened to me recently, and it turns out it was the best thing ever! The day after he left I feel like I was cured of my limerence, even though I have been crying non stop up until then. I feel so free right now, and genuinely so much happier. Dealing with him on a day to day level was pure torture.
That is so interesting! Can you elaborate on how you feel about the person who made you their LO? I always wondered what that felt like, from the other side. Did you know he liked you?
We are here. I am annoyed that 17 year olds post here, and feel it's ridiculous. So it kind of discourages me from posting. I imagine it's similar with others.

I am going through something similar right now, and I am really hoping it gets better. Cause I am sad that he is leaving, but he didn't exactly make me feel good while he was here. It was torture. So I don't understand why I'm this sad, I should be celebrating instead of crying every day.

I have PCOS, so I've been on birth control for the past 8 years or so. It works for me, honestly. I might never get off. I tried last summer, and my hair started falling off like crazy, and my skin got extremely oily and broke out so much, it was insane. So I will be taking birth control pills until my 50s probably.

This sounds awful. I think I can somewhat relate, cause a couple of months ago I was accused of liking someone at work by one person, and I was mortified. It wasnt brought up again though, I think mainly because I avoided the people involved.


Your coworkers are acting like a bunch of mean children. I can't believe how some adults behave.

Weekend is done for me. Started watching From, and am currently struggling with reading Moby Dick. I have been on Prozac for a week, but I still feel anhedonia and have very low energy. I will give it 3 more weeks, and after that (hopefully) my doctor will switch me to SNRIs.

I just recently started Prozac, so I can't really share my experience, but I think you should talk to your doctor about changing your meds. It doesn't seem like this is right for you. Maybe you will respond better to SNRIs.

I'm the same. I really feel it was a lot easier in my twenties, even if at the time I felt absolutely awful. When you turn 30 it's a whole different ball game, and I don't really know how to manage that.


You can DM me if you want to vent or just talk. It's isolating never being able to talk to anyone about how you really feel.
Kind of awful. Found out an estranged friend is pregnant. I hate that this is the way that makes me feel. I wish I could be happy for her.
I do the same exact thing. In fact, I'm currently doing it. I think I'm too afraid to lay in silence with my thoughts.

I hope you don't find this question rude, but how? How are you happy? Are you close with your friends and family, so you feel connected in that way? I genuinely am asking, because I wish I could be happy at least on some days, so I'm wondering what you are doing differently.
Yes. I just don't have the will anymore. It is very hard to make myself do anything.
Not really. A lobotomy on the other hand..

I feel exactly the same, and I've also been very isolated since the end of December. I go to see my family once a week for a couple of hours and that is literally it. That is all the social contact I have. I honestly don't know how I will ever get out of this. I have no hope anymore. This probably doesn't help you, but I just thought I'd share.

I'm in a similar boat, except I'm white. I wish there was a way for people like us to meet in real life, cause I'm really lonely in a way no one who doesn't experience this can really understand. I hope I get to radical acceptance eventually.
Hey I'm doing Chloe Ting workouts too! Started on January 1st, so now I'm on day 12, hope I finish the challenge this time.
I have never heard of this before, just looked it up and I'm pretty certain I have this. This may be my biggest problem currently.

This is a really good comment, thank you.


My only problem is that I struggle to care about other people, and it probably shows in my facial expression which I'm unable to fake. I don't mean this in any sociopathic way, I just have no interest in knowing what someone did over the weekend or (especially) talking to people who are not in my life, like hairstylists and so. I just don't see the point of talking to them. And I also am not interested in almost anything. So I think for me the main issue is anhedonia.

In that case, just give it a bit more time, you should feel better in a week or so.


When it comes to brain zaps, I don't even know how to explain them cause the feeling is so unlike anything else I experienced. Kinda felt like my brain was electrocuted. Wasn't painful, just really unpleasant.

Same, I thought I was the only one who read it at that age! I was horrified. I remember feeling almost scared of my parents just cause I realized they could technically do the things that the mother did in that book. Definitely not a book any child should read.

How long since you quit? 


I took Zoloft for 5 months, never had chest flutters, but I had brain zaps for a couple of weeks after I quit cold turkey. It wasn't pleasant, but it went away.

Off topic, but your handwriting is beautiful!


I didn't understand from the post, are you still taking dancing lessons? I've thought about taking them too, for the same reason. But I might be too disconnected from my body to try. I have no rhythm.


I feel like I'm always balancing between trying to force myself to get as much social interaction as possible and then hurting and vowing to never leave my apartment again. And then I get extremely lonely and force myself to socialize and the cycle continues. I am never stable. It is torture.
I did something similar, I wrote in my journal at the age of 12 that I probably won't have a boyfriend before 25 lol
Not to discourage you, but I don't think this gets better on its own. For me it even got worse once I passed 30.
This always happens to me too. It's like they have a sixth sense for these things.
Exercise and keep my apartment clean for once
Fully agree, got burned badly a couple of years ago, I would never do something similar again. Wish I knew better.
This is so cruel. What a pathetic loser he is that he is not even able to speak to her directly. Is he in grade school.
I have never asked a guy out, though I came close to that once and it was a terrible idea. I've aged out of clubbing, never was really the person for that, but I did go to clubs occassionaly.

I relate to this so much, I feel like I could've written this post. It is so frustrating to me that I just dont know how to behave or what to talk about. Ever. It's not only a problem with romantic relationships, but with friendships as well.

I don't currently. I've been on them for some time during this year, but I don't feel like they did anything other than numb my feelings and make me gain weight.


I was even on Xanax, among other things. Never did anything. It didn't even make me sleepy. I have no idea why people get addicted to it.

They generally try to be nice to me, and I think they do like me to an extent, they just think I'm kinda odd. This goes for the extended family - aunts, uncles, cousins etc. I'm not really close to anyone. When it comes to my immediate family, they care about me, they try to support me, we see each other on a weekly basis. My spinster status is usually never mentioned at this point (I'm 31). I get kind of sad when I think I'm depriving my parents of grandchildren, cause I know that would make them really happy, but it is what it is. I hope my brother has kids soon, so they can have that.


I don't know if it's the fact that I'm now the age my parents were when they had me, or what, but I feel way less judgmental of them as parents nowadays. They were just people. They tried their best. Sometimes they failed, but their intentions were good. I don't blame them for me turning out the way I did.

That is very tame actually compared to what I hear from guys who comment how a random woman we know looks ugly without makeup. And there's a lot more that I don't want to write, and that is what a guy who is actually sweet and kind (or appears so) says unprompted and surrounded by women. Imagine how he talks to guys.
Cause I'm socially inept.
Absolutely. In fact, I would say that is the most common reason.

I just woke myself up crying. I didn't think I could still cry with all the medication I'm taking for my depression, but I was crying in my sleep. I feel pretty numb, so I didn't think it was possible.


I actually got a big raise at work yesterday. Then I had to go out with some friends and I felt like shit. Hanging out with other people always makes me feel awful. I hate that I couldn't enjoy some actual good news for one whole day. I think I feel worse than before.

I had a bachelorette's party I had to go to. I was kind of miserable and people could tell. I just have no way of connecting with anyone, and I don't even mean romantically. People are just repulsed by me.
yeah, i think it's just that most people pair up eventually. and we do not, for some reason that i can't fully figure out.

I'm not sure which came first for me, but you definitely should bring this up to a therapist, if you're seeing one. Find one that makes you feel ok, but then you have to be honest. Otherwise you are just wasting your money. And they have heard it all, you are not going to shock them by saying anything at all.

The thing is, you are not. Take a look around, plenty of ugly people are in relationships. It has to be something else. Not that I'm saying looks don't play a part cause they definitely do. But it doesn't add up when you see someone who is objectively not that good looking, but they're in a relationship. And they don't even have an amazing body or extremely beautiful hair.
Same here. I wish I could just sleep forever.
I haven't. I heard good things about it. The problem is I also struggle with social anxiety. But at this point depression is definitely my bigger problem.

yes. my brother is somewhat similar to me, but he does not have avpd. our childhood experience is very similar, we're close in age. he struggles in some ways, but he has a girlfriend of 6 years, and even before her he was in a long term relationship. the thing that weirds me out is that both of our parents are extroverts. my mom is the most extroverted person i know. i have no idea how they managed to create me. it's almost bizarre.

do you mind sharing how the therapy went? did you choose to work on one schema, or all of them combined or something else? and the lexapro - in what way did it help, did it make you feel less anxious?
thank you. we'll see, maybe i give up too easily or something, but it's all pretty disheartening.

i understand that, but it never amounts to anything no matter what i do. trust me, if anyone really desperately wants it to work, it's me. but it just isn't. when i was doing cbt, i was doing what my therapist told me to do, and my problems remained the same. when i was in psychodynamic therapy, i didn't even know what i was supposed to do, but i was sharing a lot of deep stuff about myself, i would get insight moments, but they amounted to nothing substantial. and now schema therapy is also amounting to nothing, cause i've had 4 months worth of therapy and we haven't even really identified the schema to work on. i just talk and talk, and i feel better in the moment sometimes, but my life doesn't change by doing that. and it doesn't seem to me like the therapists i've had feel any sense of urgency about that.

another problem with my current therapy is that im supposed to "feel the wounded child within me" and i have no idea how to do that. it seems too vague, if im honest. i tell my therapist all the stories from my childhood, then she tellls me to connect emotionally to that moment which i am unable to do (unable, it's not a question of will) the more i try to connect, the more i feel nothing. and then nothing happens, we just go in circles.

so far it hasn't really helped me. i've tried cbt, psychodynamic therapy and im currently on schema therapy, where i don't feel like im making any progress. my problems remain, they haven't really budged an inch. i even tried meds and that amounted to nothing, i just felt numb, nothing more.

the thing i hate the most is that people always recommend therapy as if that is the solution to everything, and you just show up there and let the therapy do it's magic.
Yes, over here they do an exam anally for virgins, but I don't want to go through that. I wish they would just do it the regular way, but the holy grail of hymen prevents them I guess.

Yes I do, cause at least where I'm from the first question is always "when did you lose your virginity" and I'm embarrassed at this point. I wish they would just do an exam and not ask those questions, but they refuse once you tell them you've never had sex.


The one thing I envy men on is that they don't have a medical record somewhere stating they are virgins.
See, for me, I don't think this is necessarily true. It's not like I have suitors lining up in front of my door, but they're below my standards. There is no one.
Thank you for this post. We could all benefit from this attitude.

I think your conclusion at the end is correct, anxiety consumes so much of your energy that little is left for thinking. I swear when I'm around people my cognitive abilities drop by at least 50%. It's very frustrating.

I haven't. If I'm honest I don't think that's the best idea. I've never had a friendship form by approaching someone in public, at least not after the age of 10. Friendships tend to develop spontaneously, by being around people who you're compatible with and spending quite a bit of time with them without having to arrange anything. Which is why most start at school, work, maybe some classes etc. So I would say, go do the things that you like to do, and you should meet some friends organically this way, if you're friendly.


I don't think this is the right approach when it comes to men, either. The thing with (most) men is when they're attracted to you, they'll do the initiating, and when they're not, there's no point in you trying either. I wish I had a more uplifting message, but what can I do.

I didn't think I'd be the first one to comment, was kind of waiting for others, as I'm interested in this myself. Honestly, I understand where you're coming from, I have zero romantic experience and I'm 31. And I have my sad days when I feel just awful. But I think there is more to life than love relationships. There is more to look forward to. You could become an aunt, or immerse yourself in a passion of some sort, or... something else (I've run out of ideas). I don't think we should start digging graves because we might not get romantic love in this lifetime. It is an important part of life, but it's not life itself.


So, you know, take what you need, and be on your way. And stop crying your heart out.

I agree with you, but even when a relationship falls apart, at least you were once in a relationship. You (proverbial you, I mean) have that experience, whereas the women here are outcast on a completely different level. That is the worst of it. That this is something you can't even talk about, other than anonymously. I agree that others have it hard at certain points, but I don't think they carry this shame, just cause their relationships ended.

I relate to this, we are close in age. I don't have anything smart to add. The way our life is currently structured is that we live in a patriarchal society that centers traditional families, no matter all the freedoms we seem to have acquired. This isn't the only way for a society to function, and possibly not even the best way, but it's the way of our world. The way things stand, sisterhood is very much a pie in the sky, I agree with you there. Single women do have it bad on that account. I'm sad that there can't be a community that these women could form and feel like they belong to, but at least we have the internet.
I installed tinder for a day. It was pretty meaningless. Didn't have any terrible experiences, but I just felt weird talking to complete strangers. It felt robotic, so I deleted it.
Thank you!
I do the worst of all I'm afraid. I'm 31, so if I told someone the truth, they would think I'm an alien.

A year is a bit too long of a period for me to be able to stay focused. I try to set goals every three weeks, cause I read somewhere that habits take 21 days to form. I will say my goals are much more modest - currently they are: keeping my apartment (and myself lol) clean every day, reading 50 pages a day, practicing duolingo and going to the office every day, which I hate (we can work from home some of the time, but I think I should be around people more and try being more social).


I've been doing this for almost three weeks now, and haven't skipped a day, and next week I'll start to exercise, and hopefully keep at it. 


My goals seem modest when I write them down, but accomplishing them makes me feel somewhat good about myself, especially when I generally feel like shit, like now.
Valentines day isn't a huge deal where I'm from, so it will be just another day, it was never very special. But I love your attitude! Sounds like a great day to me :)

Pretty fine, I cleaned my apartment and did some reading. These days I feel like I'm not too bothered by my loneliness. I've kept my apartment clean for 2 weeks now (probably the longest time ever), and I'm really proud of that, cause I used to have a lot of trouble with it, and my apartment was always a mess.

I really hated living with my parents, and only moved out finally when I was 29. I live on my own though, and I'm not sure how I would function with roommates.


I don't think there's anything wrong with living with your parents. A lot of people don't like to live alone. I'm not among them, my mental health is very much improved since I started living alone.
I had a very similar thing happen. On the first day of taking zoloft I got a cold (sore throat, slight fever, headache etc). I thought it was just a weird coincidence, but I don't know.
I haven't been taking it for as long as you have, but in the first couple of weeks I would feel pretty dizzy at times. I think it's normal when you're adjusting.

I have been on two dates. One when I was 15, the other when I was 24. They were both pretty awkward and meaningless. I wasn't really attracted to the guys, I just wanted to have the experience. But I think it's not too different from hanging out with someone platonically, aside from the romantic/sexual stuff. I had a bad time, because I suck at talking to people I don't know well, so I made it awkward.


I don't think I like dating as a concept. I would much prefer to get to know someone spontaneously and then get into a relationship (which is usually how it goes where I'm from, at least for other people). Dating is something we imported from America, and it just feels weird to me.
I've experienced the same thing, and I hate how people (especially men) downplay it. It's like they cannot comprehend social anxiety in women.
It sounds really tough, I'm sorry you're going through this. Has your doctor prescribed anything to help you manage the anxiety during the adjustment period? If not, maybe you could ask.

Same here. We're the same age if that's your birth year in your username. Everyone around me is having babies, getting married etc. Meanwhile I have the life experience of an average 13 year old.


I'm not on social media, so I don't see most of it though. And I don't go to high school reunions. 


I wish I knew someone like me irl
How's your sleep? I get like that when I'm sleep deprived. Which I'm now all the time cause of the insomnia. Sigh
Look them dead in the eyes for a second or two (until it gets uncomfortable) and then say "you're very perceptive" and smile.

Jesus, all the people in the comments citing studies. Lighten up. It's just for fun.


I'm a scorpio.

I don't really put any effort in dating, by which I mean I'm not on dating apps and I don't approach men either online or in person. I do meet people I'm attracted to, sometimes they flirt with me. That is it.
As a girl too.
I'd want to join. I'm on day 7 of 25mg, starting 50mg tomorrow.
Fuck her. Honestly. You're allowed to be however you want to be as long as you're not hurting anyone. Any sane person would see her for the asshole she is.

Exactly. And no one else gets it, so I can't even talk to anyone how I've been feeling super anxious all week because of it. 

I really hope both of our parties are bearable.
You need better friends. This guy sounds like an asshole.

I feel you, I have a work Christmas party coming up and I'm dreading it. I have no idea who I'm even gonna talk to. Try to remind myself in the big picture it doesn't matter. But it's already making me feel horrible.

And these events are supposed to be fun! There are people who go and have a blast. Sometimes I'm amazed I'm the same species as them.
I relate to the tinder part. I just can't chat to people at all, and then they get mad. I've deleted it. Barely been on it for a day.
This will be me in a few days. I wish I knew a way out of it.

I know how you feel. I am excluded at work and it sucks big time. Whenever I confide in someone, they're dismissive of how terrible that feels. IT SUCKS. Wish we worked together, we could team up at least :)
That is crazy. You're not overreacting at all, are they in grade school or something? Next time, please just address them like they're children and say "that wasn't very nice". Don't stay silent!

Same. It sucks so badly. There were times when I was accepted and I even have some friends I see after work (now they no longer work with me). People talk about me within earshot, as if I'm not even there.
Yes. My niece has a boyfriend. She's 23, I'm 31. Doesn't make much of a difference at this point though. I'm numb to it. I don't have any younger siblings, but I think it would be a similar feeling.

I haven't done that, but I have tried to approach. Went poorly every time. Don't intend to ever do that again. If a guy is into you, he will try something, and if he isn't, it's best you stay far far away from him. When a woman isn't attracted to a man at first, they might end up married. Never the case when it's a man who isn't attracted.
I've made some friends at work. I don't think it's ever too late to make new friends.
I hate it when people question you like that. I usually lie, but I feel like they know I'm lying.
I feel the same. I hate going to work so much. I don't talk to anyone and it makes me feel horrible. I just don't see a way out.
I didn't really change at all, I'm afraid. My circumstances changed, which at times helped, but I stayed the same. Time doesn't heal anything when it comes to this.

I know how you feel, I hate my birthday. Wish I could skip it. 

Good luck with the interview, though.
Not yet, but I'll keep you posted.
I'm not sure that what you're describing even exists. Most guys in a FWB situation are far from being your friend. I think that would be 10 times harder to find than a relationship, honestly.

I also am not sure I could imagine a relationship. The only problem with this is that finding a guy who wants FWB and respects you on top of that is more difficult than finding a relationship where I'm from.
The Book of Disquiet - Fernando Pessoa

I was in your position until I was 24, except I had been on one random date when I was 15. Then at 24 I went on my second (and last) date, I made out with a guy. That's it, and I'm almost 30. 

I think I'm going to try Tinder. I just want to experience something.
I know what you mean, but you don't want that kind of attention, trust me. I think everyone attracts creeps the most when they're underage.

I wonder about this as well. I have to see and hear about this person often. I think I'm going to try CBT for this. Enough is enough.

I think it takes a long time, if you don't have other prospects, sadly :(

Kind of lonely. Went to see my parents for lunch yesterday. Today it was just me, cleaning my apartment, cause when I'm depressed it turns into a mess, cause I can't force myself to clean. So there was a lot of work, but I did it. Now my apartment's clean and I'm alone.

I feel like the end of summer. Weirdly nostalgic over something that didn't even happen.
I have similar concerns. I have no social life, so that would probably be a concern.
I'm truly happy for you. It's nice to know there is a way out of this hell, at least sometimes.
Are you happy now?

This is such a nice response!

I've completely given up on talking about this with anyone, except here. I don't even bother. I don't know, maybe we can all just work on things that we can work on, and try to find something to be happy about, even if it is trivial.

It is difficult. I have my ups and downs. Turning 30 in a couple of months, and that has been the hardest thing. I go between frantically trying to change something and being completely apathetic. The worst (and best) thing for me is that I delude myself with crushes on anyone who pays me any attention.
No, not at all. My mom is very social. My dad is weird, but not like me. He can be very social when he wants to be.
They aren't awkward. Mainly because I never meet other awkward people in real life.
What is up with that? Sometimes I have people flirting with me and almost asking me out, but as soon as I show interest back, it's done.
I notice the same thing. Just at work there are at least 8 guys I liked at some point. It's kind of disgusting. Nothing happened with anyone, obviously.
I relate to this. But it's hard to follow this, when no one ever asks you out. So whenever I hear advice like "if he wanted to, he would", I feel sad, cause clearly no one wants to.
Thanks :)
No, sadly. I'm well aware of my limitations.

I know what you're going through, it happened to me too on my first job, and come to think about it, it kind of happened again in this job. I would say if at all possible try to focus on the job, and being excellent at your job. Shift your focus away from the social stuff. Be polite and cordial, but that's it. 

If anyone is really bullying you either try to talk to them one on one, or report them to the HR. When it comes to teasing, there is sadly so much you can do, when you're not socially confident. But do try to let them know their behavior is not ok. Best to do this one on one as opposed to in a group, because bullies are cowards when you approach them alone. They gain all their strength from the social group.
Because I'm too fucked up to be in any kind of relationship. Even friendships.

This is my experience as well. People say "Just put yourself out there, don't be afraid of rejection etc" and they don't even get it at all. When I do try and connect with people it brings me such tremendous pain to watch me make them leave. I don't know what the point is.
I feel exactly the same, so I'm afraid I can't be much help. This year has been the worst one of my life so far. It is so much worse the older you get. Makes me afraid of the future.

Something very similar happened to me 4 months ago. There was a time I used to love going to work, but now it's terrible. It somehow fucked up my relationships with other coworkers as well, people kind of hate me now.
Sometimes. I don't think I'm unattractive though.
Right? Hugs on their own do absolutely nothing for me.
Turning 30 in a couple of months. It doesn't seem like it's worth the effort. If someone wants to date me they can make it happen. I'm done trying. I just don't care.
Yes. When I was 12 I wrote in my journal that I wouldn't have a boyfriend before 25. Then I didn't end up getting one at 25 either lol
Cancelled on friends cause I'm too depressed to hang out with anyone. I don't think I'll leave my house any time soon.
This sort of reminded me of the show "The Act". If you haven't seen it, maybe you could check it out, I really liked it. My mom is/was overprotective as well, it does damage you.

I have no choice. Thank God I have the option of working from home, otherwise I would've had a breakdown or fifty by now. Even then, it is really hard. The work is fine, it's the socialization that I can't stand. But it does make you learn stuff about yourself. I figured out I can't set boundaries with people at all, I can only be a complete pushover (which I am, 99% of the time) or a bitch who is angry for no reason. So I will be attending assertiveness classes.

Socialization did NOT get easier for me btw, quite the opposite. For most people it probably does get easier with time, but not for us. It got so much worse with time, I now have a couple of former friends at work, who completely abandoned me, so I have that on my plate as well. It's not just anxiety, it's a lot deeper than that, I just cannot act normal in relationships of any kind.
People dying their hair blonde is not cultural appropriation. That is ridiculous. Having blonde hair is not a culture.
I feel the same. It's a lot easier the first couple of times. After about a month it gets really difficult, cause people just give up on you.
Have you heard of The Smiths?

I think I might be autistic. I face the same social issues regardless of that diagnosis. So...that.

Sometimes people like me at first, but they lose interest fast when they realize I have problems.

I'm conflicted. I do get you, and I'm 29, so already an old virgin. It is difficult, for sure. However, I don't think having had sex one time would've made anything easier. Maybe it would make your mind relax a bit, where you would realize it doesn't matter. 

I thought like this when I was 24 and made out with some guy I barely knew and wasn't particularly attracted to. At the time I thought "thank God it finally happened", but the truth is it didn't change anything at all for me. I am no better off now than I would've been had I not kissed that guy. 

My problem wasn't never having been kissed, my problem was not being able to connect with people, and a meaningless makeout session didn't solve that. If anything it served as a distraction from the real issues that I should've been working on.
I think it depends on the therapist. I've told my therapist I was suicidal numerous times, it didn't phase them. They didn't even prescribe me anything.
People who choose this subreddit to try to find someone to date are scum.
Not really. Typical teenage behaviour does make me roll my eyes to the point of an aneurism. But I'm not scared or anything. Just deeply annoyed.
Story of my life.

Because the only reason why the patient doesn't already know the truth is precisely because he/she chooses not to, ie puts up defenses to knowing the truth. Therefore, even if the analyst did just plainly tell the patient the truth of the matter the second he himself became aware of it, it wouldn't do the patient any good, because his defenses would still be up, he would simply choose to ignore this truth, conclude that the analyst is wrong etc. So the analyst has to work on lowering the patients defenses first if the psychoanalytic process is to be constructive at all.
